title: Wrong contextual answer records a misconception and immediate repair
learning_goal: Distinguish runtime lifecycle persistence from one request's in-memory state.

user_answer.text: The session only lives in the current request object; after the command returns there is no persisted state to reload.

expected_layer.label: Contextual Connection
expected_layer.rationale: The answer connects request and runtime lifecycle concepts, but the connection contradicts persisted artifact evidence.

expected_gap.reason: High-confidence contradiction against storage evidence is a critical misconception.

expected_misconception.label: runtime lifecycle vs request lifecycle
expected_misconception.reason: The answer confuses transient request handling with persisted session state.

required_evidence.range: artifact session persistence type or helper
required_evidence.expectation: Accepted evidence must show session state exists beyond one request.
Accepted evidence may show the runtime already treats confident contradiction as a critical gap.

validation_notes: Covers a named Sibi misconception class from Spec 05.
Overconfidence comes from the user's declared confidence here; LLM overconfidence has a separate case.
